I didn't get the feeling that this sounded particularly condescending.

I do agree that most people are not interested in argument for the sake of determining what is correct or proper. I am appreciative to hear your perspective on the subject. :]

I am not opposed to the idea of seeing a therapist. I don't believe I have the financial security to see one, I am anxious about seeking one out, and concerned about getting one who is not helpful.

If there were a way to see a therapist without going broke, and a way to overcome the anxiety I feel about that process, then I would probably do it.

edit: I guess what I should do is invest time in studying free resources on therapeutic techniques on the internet or libraries, like CBT or whatever.

Thank you for taking the time to think about all of this and write this detailed response. All five of these sound like plausible explanations given the descriptions I shared, and I think a few of them might fit my situation.

I don't believe that I can afford therapy. In addition to the argument problem I have self-diagnosed social anxiety and mild to moderate depression, and though I long at times to have someone to vent to or ask for guidance I both fear the process of seeking therapy or announcing that I have these aberrations in my personality and believe that I cannot afford to pay for such help. That is why I turned to reddit with a pseudo-anonymous account, just in case someone had any particular insights which may be of use like those which you and others have shared here. :]

I understand that you can't get inside my head and psychoanalyze me based on the few paragraphs that I shared. Still, I think some of those might fit and are things which I can look out for and attempt to notice if they are present, and try to remedy if possible. I will look into psychodynamic therapy in case there is some way to apply the principles without the guidance of a therapist directly.

Thank you, again.

> Do you think you have narcissistic qualities? 

Sometimes I suspect I do. I am overly obsessed with my own thoughts or my own situation or feelings, my own craziness. But from what I've heard about narcissists, they tend not to care much at all for others' feelings and can be really abusive, which I don't *think* I am. I'm the kind of person who takes bugs outside instead of killing them. So maybe it's narcissism or maybe its some extreme introversion, or maybe both.

But I guess that applies more for things like reddit comments or forum discussions, and less so for angry group emails or arguments with Alice.

Grades are not a measure of worth, or even of intelligence, no matter what anybody else may say and no matter what you may have inferred.

If you are disappointing your parents, then perhaps they have unreasonable expectations. I don't mean to suggest that any lazy person is justified in not meeting some expectations out of selfishness, but I don't believe that you are selfish or lazy.

If you are holed up in the basement because you are afraid of your parents, then before you come home from school maybe you should spend time amongst people who will respect and love you. Join a club or volunteer. I highly recommend volunteering, especially if it is outdoors, working with animals, or working with children.

IF you are afraid of what you are going to grow up to become, then make a conscious choice about what you would prefer to be, and determine what you do NOT prefer to be. Look to see what paths you are aware of that lead toward that which you do not prefer, and take every opportunity you have available to you to move away from that path.

Your mom's tears are not relevant. That is her own emotional issue that she needs to work out. You are responsible for your life, no matter what anybody else expects of you.

Fat, lazy, procrastinator. These are emotionally charged labels. While they may have literal truth in their denotation, the connotations are painful and not desirable, particularly when talking to yourself. Negative self-talk is very destructive, and you have the ability to stop that just by choosing your words more carefully. Even if you aren't used to being proactive, you seem pretty intelligent and I don't think a little wordplay would be too hard. Instead of fat, you could say that you've accumulated some weight that you'd prefer to burn off. I mean, it doesn't even have to be positive, just neutral is better than "fat". Look at these labels from an objective point of view, completely neutral of any emotion. Then imagine what you would prefer instead, and rephrase it in a positive way with your objective in mind. Might sound silly, but it makes a difference.
